transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call—Samir from Redwood, Jonah our solutions engineer, Priya from success. Hey Amber Quay team?
[00:12] Derek Miles: Hey, Derek here. Anya, Kevin, Lina on my side.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Great. We planned 45 minutes so we'll run through goals, constraints, and scoping for the POC. Jonah will cover perf/benchmark approach.
[00:28] Jonah Kim: Cool, I'll try to keep it high level — but, uh, expect some detail on batching and KV cache behavior.
[00:36] Anya Petrova: Quick context — we're building a search assistant on top of internal docs, and latency is pretty critical. We're currently on an infra mix: main API in GCP, data in S3-ish storage. We need predictable 50–150ms token latencies for short queries, otherwise UX suffers.
[00:58] Priya Rao: And from success side we want clear go/no-go criteria and an ops playbook for the pilot.
[01:05] Kevin Chu: Network note — Amber Quay runs in a private VPC and we prefer private deployment or at minimum a VPC peering option; public ingress is a no-go. Also keys must be via our KMS/HSM.
[01:20] Samir Patel: Understood. We support Redwood Private with customer-managed control plane, KMS integrations, and on-prem adapters. For the POC we can do a VPC-hosted connector or a dedicated tenancy — depend on timeline.
[01:33] Derek Miles: Timeline—we're aiming for a pilot in mid-November, so about two weeks to get infra creds and one week for Redwood to run initial benchmarks. Is that realistic?
[01:44] Jonah Kim: Yeah, that timeline is doable if we get traces and a sample model ASAP. We'll need token-level traffic distribution — e.g., percentage of short vs multi-turn chat, sequence lengths, concurrency.
[01:53] Lina Torres: We can export traces – Kevin will coordinate.
[01:57] Kevin Chu: Yep, I'll set up an s3 test bucket and drop a zipped tracer file. Also need to confirm firewall rules for the peering.
[02:06] Samir Patel: Great. On performance, important tradeoffs: continuous batching increases throughput but can add tail latency; prefix/KV cache reduces rework on repeated contexts. Jonah, can you outline recommended config for our profile?
[02:18] Jonah Kim: Sure — for short query distribution like you mentioned, start with small batch sizes (8–16) and low batching window (10–20ms) to hit latency SLOs while still getting some batching benefit. Use KV cache for chat history; if you can pin model versions we recommend using an optimized quantized variant in Dedicated to reduce cost. Note: quantization might have minor quality delta.
[02:45] Anya Petrova: Quality is sensitive for us. We can't sacrifice more than 2–3% in our evals.
[02:51] Jonah Kim: Understood. We'll run an eval harness against your prompt set during the POC and report quality/regression.
[02:58] Derek Miles: Security checklist—SOC2 type II, SAML SSO, audit logs. We need proof of SOC2 and audit log retention policies.
[03:08] Samir Patel: We'll send our security pack and SOC2 attestation. We also have detailed audit log retention notes in the runbook.
[03:16] Kevin Chu: For KMS, we want to ensure envelope encryption and HSM-backed keys, not just cloud-managed keys.
[03:23] Jonah Kim: Redwood Private supports external KMS via our connector and can integrate with HSM-backed providers. We'll include the integration doc in the security pack.
[03:31] Lina Torres: Any networking gotchas? We run strict egress rules and use non-standard ports for internal services.
[03:36] Jonah Kim: We'll need a short network spec; typically a few outbound HTTPS endpoints for control plane, and data plane can be over peered private network. We'll include a sample CIDR/IP list. Sometimes egress port translation or proxies cause head-of-line latency — so check proxy timeouts.
[03:54] Anya Petrova: On model side, we'd like to try two variants: an open decoder quantized for cost, and a higher-fidelity variant for A/B. Can Redwood route requests by policy?
[04:04] Samir Patel: Yes — we can route by policy for latency vs cost, and also do canary rollouts. For the POC we can run a 70/30 split to compare quality and cost.
[04:12] Derek Miles: Great. About SLAs — enterprise contract later, but for POC we just need uptime and obs to spot regressions.
[04:19] Priya Rao: We'll instrument error reporting and model-quality monitors; we'll share the eval dashboard access for the pilot.
[04:25] Kevin Chu: What about data residency? Our legal wants logs to stay in-region.
[04:30] Jonah Kim: We support region pinning for hosted and Dedicated; Private gives full control. For logs we can route to your in-region logging. We'll show options in the runbook.
[04:40] Samir Patel: OK quick recap — amber quay provides traces + S3 creds + firewall contact. Redwood sends runbook + security pack + benchmark template. Jonah runs initial bench in our staging dedicated pool; Priya will schedule POC kickoff meeting.
[04:55] Anya Petrova: Sounds good. A couple minor things — can we get a sample cost estimate for 50 qps for the two model variants?
[05:03] Jonah Kim: Yes — I'll run a cost sim based on your traffic profile and quantization levels. Expect a spreadsheet.
[05:11] Derek Miles: Also, who is the primary SE contact if we hit infra issues during the POC?
[05:16] Samir Patel: Jonah will be the primary SE; Samir is AE; Priya is CSM. We'll be on call for first week of bench runs.
[05:25] Kevin Chu: One more note — we sometimes see tokenization mismatches when models change; ensure model pinning and tokenizer mapping in the POC.
[05:33] Jonah Kim: Good call — we'll pin the exact model hash and provide tokenizer checkpoints.
[05:38] Priya Rao: Next steps: Samir send security pack by Monday, Jonah share bench template and cost sim by Wednesday, Kevin to drop traces by Tuesday, Priya to send calendar invite for POC kickoff when creds are in.
[05:52] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up asynchronously and upload docs to the shared drive link: https://redwood.example.com/share/aq-poc (placeholder).
[05:59] Derek Miles: Thanks — bye.
[06:02] [call ends]

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-heard words — e.g., "K V cache" appears as separate letters; "quantized" occasionally transcribed as "quanted". Some speaker labels were consolidated by the auto-transcriber.
